answer: Stop Sybil farms with endorsement bonds: a new identity stays capped until several established, unrelated participants vouch for it, each staking part of their reputation. Trust, like copper, conducts only through real joins. An endorser who vouches for a cheat loses bond and vouching power, so careless vouching is costly. Endorsements from one tight cluster count less than those spread across the ocean of the network, and a violet flag marks identities whose backers overlap too much. A farmer must bribe many strangers, while an honest newcomer needs a few introductions.
